name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Bill Keating running with a large cash advantage
Polymarket prices Keating at 96% to win
Republican challenger has modest fundraising and no outside support
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Keating: a D+6 district, incumbency, a big fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing him near certain. With no contrary polling or ratings, the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 19 points.
model.watch: A late polling surprise or an unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising surge would be the main signals to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about six points. He has raised over $420,000 and holds nearly $500,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised less and trails badly in cash. No independent groups are spending in the race, and no general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets give Keating roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the seat as competitive. With a favorable environment for Democrats layered on top of the district's lean and incumbency, the race sits comfortably in Safe D territory, with the main uncertainty being the exact size of the margin rather than the winner.
